chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Bandar narrated to us, saying: Abul Abbas al-Himadi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sayyagh narrated to us, saying: Al-Qa'nabi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Dhi'eb narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "It is not permissible for a Muslim to forsake his brother for more than three days."

key_terms.يُهْجِرَ: to forsake or cut off ties (socially or verbally)

ai.seo_question: What is the maximum duration a Muslim can ignore his brother before it becomes impermissible?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* codifies the maximum duration of permissible estrangement (*hijr*) to prevent minor disputes from escalating into lasting rifts. It reflects the Shia emphasis on *sulh* (reconciliation) as a superior act of worship, urging the aggrieved party to initiate peace after three days to preserve communal harmony and spiritual purity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-250 Muhammad ibn Ja’far al-Bandar narrated that Abul Abbas al-Himady quoted Muhammad ibn Ali al-Zayeq, on the authority of Al-Qa’nabi , on the authority of Ibn Abi Za’eb , on the authority of Ibn Shahab, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “It is not allowed for one to be on no talking terms with his Muslim brother for more than three days.”
